description: Congresswoman Judy Chu (CA-27), Chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC), is seeking a highly motivated, detail-orientated, and energetic individual to assist with communications, digital media and social media, and graphic design as a press fellow in the D.C. office. This is a four-month paid position that reports to the Communications Director. Daily tasks include drafting and posting content for the member's social media platforms and website; graphic design; daily press clips; drafting press releases, newsletters, and advisories; and organizing press events. The ideal candidate will be creative, politically astute, have a strong proficiency in crafting social media content across social media platforms, and will be a detail-oriented team player able to handle multiple tasks at once. Excellent writing and strong organizational skills are essential, along with the ability to be a self-starter while working in a fast-paced environment.
responsibilities: Drafting and posting content for the member's social media platforms and website
Drafting press releases, newsletters, and advisories
qualifications: Highly motivated, detail-orientated, and energetic
Creative and politically astute
Strong proficiency in crafting social media content across social media platforms
Detail-oriented team player able to handle multiple tasks at once
Excellent writing skills
Strong organizational skills
Ability to be a self-starter while working in a fast-paced environment
how_to_apply: Qualified candidates should submit a cover letter, resume, one writing sample, and one example of previous digital media or graphic design products to Ben.Suarato@mail.house.gov with "Press Fellow" in the subject line. No phone calls, faxes, or drop-ins please.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer; we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin or citizenship status, sex, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, sexual orientation, age, disability, or military status.

description: The Democratic staff of the House Committee on Oversight and Reform, Subcommittee on Government Operations, is seeking an energetic and self-motivated graduate student for a full-time internship for Spring 2022. The position offers the opportunity to gain substantive experience on an exciting and fast-paced Subcommittee, while participating directly in the oversight process and learning about the day-to-day operations of the House of Representatives. The Committee on Oversight and Reform is the primary investigative committee of the U.S. House of Representatives, with jurisdiction to investigate any matter at any time. The Subcommittee on Government Operations has jurisdiction over issues related to the federal civil service, whistleblower protections, the U.S. Postal Service; government management and accounting measures; the economy, efficiency, and management of government operations and activities; government reorganization; intergovernmental affairs, including state and local governments; federal information technology security, acquisition policy, and management; and federal property.
responsibilities: Assisting staff in preparing for congressional hearings
Attending various briefings and meetings with Executive Branch and private sector officials
Working closely with Committee counsel and staff
qualifications: Interest in public service
Desire to learn
Superior attention to detail
Work well under pressure
Self-motivated
Excellent written and oral communication skills
Willing to be in the office full time
Graduate student
how_to_apply: Email resume and cover letter in one PDF titled "last name, first name, Spring 2022 GovOps" to Government.Operations@mail.house.gov with "Spring 2022 Internship Application" in the subject line. No phone calls or drop-ins please. Only applicants who are selected for an interview will receive a response.

description: Team Moulton is seeking exceptional students interested in foreign policy and national security to participate in the Fern Holland International Affairs Fellowship Program. This is a full-time, paid foreign policy fellowship for Summer 2022. This opportunity is based on financial need and is only open to candidates who are Pell-grant eligible. The fellowship is in our Washington, D.C. office. Current undergraduate students, recent college graduates, and students currently enrolled in graduate school are eligible. Team Moulton is looking for hard-working individuals who are passionate, driven, and committed to strengthening our democracy. This fully-funded fellowship covers the cost of housing, transportation, and food with a stipend. Women, People of Color, and members of other underrepresented communities are especially encouraged to apply. This fellowship offers an in-depth look into a career of service to our nation. Fellows will be expected to perform rigorous research, advise senior staff and the Congressman on important issues, and craft policies in international affairs and national security, in addition to some regularly assigned intern responsibilities. If selected, you will be required to submit a FAFSA form. We are accepting applications for Summer through March 15, 2022.

qualifications: Pell-grant eligible
Current undergraduate student, recent college graduate, or currently enrolled in graduate school
Hard-working, passionate, driven, and committed to strengthening our democracy
Interested in foreign policy and national security
how_to_apply: Fill out the internship application form at moulton.house.gov under the 'Services' tab and attach a cover letter and resume. If you have trouble accessing the application form, email grace.curtiss@mail.house.gov. Applications accepted through March 15, 2022.

description: The House Judiciary Committee Democratic staff are looking for interns for the summer semester. The House Committee on the Judiciary's staff internship program offers undergraduate students, law students, graduate students, and recent graduates an opportunity to experience the operation of a congressional committee firsthand and learn about the important role that our Committee plays in the legislative process. The Judiciary Committee has jurisdiction over a wide range of legislative and oversight issues, including oversight of the U.S. Department of Justice, constitutional law, federal criminal law, voting rights, immigration and naturalization, intellectual property law, and antitrust law. Stipends will be available to summer interns. Intern assignments will vary depending on the work of the Judiciary Committee each semester. The deadline to apply for the summer semester is February 15, 2022. This internship is based in Washington, DC.
responsibilities: Researching policy issues under the committee's jurisdiction
Attending briefings and hearings on the Hill
Supporting committee clerks and professional staff members
Providing administrative support, including answering calls, delivering correspondence, and setting up the hearing room
qualifications: Must be an undergraduate student, law student, graduate student, or recent graduate
Interest in the legislative process and congressional committee operations
Interest in issues under the Judiciary Committee's jurisdiction such as constitutional law, federal criminal law, voting rights, immigration, intellectual property law, and antitrust law
how_to_apply: To learn more and apply, please visit https://judiciary.house.gov/about/internshipopportunities.htm. The deadline to apply for the summer semester is February 15, 2022.
equal_opportunity: The Committee does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including marital or parental status, sexual orientation, and gender identity), disability, age, or national origin.
